title: Angular Material (AngularJS) documentation website, 2016
lede: The 2016 home page of Google’s Material library for AngularJS, with a blue side navigation and flat gray tiles.
summary: Blue side navigation with all-capital items, a pale gray header bar, and flat gray tiles with Material icons. 2016.

evidence.note: Captured with `tools/capture.mjs` (headless Chrome, 1440 × 900) on 28 September 2026 and inspected. The screenshot shows the first viewport; the measurement covers up to four screens.

styles.note: Clear example of a Material 1 documentation layout: a saturated blue navigation drawer, all-capital medium labels, Material system icons, Roboto, and a header bar that casts a thin shadow. The tiles themselves are flat.

notice: The live site now documents the end of long-term support for AngularJS Material, which ended in January 2022.
observed: A blue navigation drawer on the left holds a red Angular shield, the name “Angular Material” in white, and sections in white all-capital labels with small chevrons.
A pale gray header bar reads “Introduction” and casts a thin shadow over the white content area.
The content is Roboto on white, with four flat light gray tiles (GETTING STARTED, DEMOS, CUSTOMIZATION, API REFERENCE), each with a gray Material icon and an all-capital label.
Links in the tiles are a red-pink accent color.
interpretation: The page measures shadows on only 8 % of its boxes, with a median blur of 7.5 px and offset of 2 px. Most of its boxes are flat gray tiles and navigation rows, so the shadow share falls far below the specimen.
borrow: Put navigation on the primary color and content on white, and use gray tiles with a single icon and an all-capital label for primary links.

images.alt: Angular Material documentation in 2016: a blue left navigation with a red Angular shield logo and all-capital section labels, a gray header bar reading Introduction, and flat gray tiles with icons for Getting started, Demos, Customization, and API reference.
images.caption: [Wayback Machine copy of material.angularjs.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20160529050309/https://material.angularjs.org/latest/), 29 May 2016.
